seed: Two menu rows advertise a key: Layer > Delete Layer shows Command Delete and Edit > Fill with Foreground shows Option Delete. Both chords were dead, because SwiftUI's own .delete is a character no Mac keyboard sends. This asks the menu bar which item really carries each chord, and runs what the press means.

steps.note: a drawn rectangle over the background, picked on its own: two layers, and Layer > Delete Layer shows Command Delete beside it
THE FIRST TEST: the chord Layer > Delete Layer shows is really on that row, so Command Delete means dropping the picked layer and nothing else. The rectangle is gone and one layer is left
undo puts the rectangle back, so nothing the chord did is one way
an empty new layer with a marquee drawn on it, and Edit > Fill with Foreground showing Option Delete beside it
THE SECOND TEST: Option Delete is really Edit > Fill with Foreground, so the marquee comes back flooded with the foreground colour rather than nothing happening at all
